text: Emit a replay capsule next to every repair: exact input bytes, working directory, bounded command, and raw exit transcript.
rationale: At 3am the failure is rerunnable offline without rebuilding a fixture or trusting a paraphrased status.

text: Make boundary fixtures literal byte strings with names that state their post-truncation length, including 512-in/508-out cases.
rationale: The numbers become visible at construction time, so cap arithmetic cannot silently drift between worker repair and parent acceptance.

text: Replace one-off shell diagnostics with a tiny python -m verifier that reads a capsule and exits with the original command status.
rationale: No heredoc quoting or environment guesswork is needed, while raw exits and finite process ownership stay intact.

text: Let a worker hand off its exact verification command and working directory as data, and have acceptance execute that command without reconstructing it.
rationale: Routing and custody remain explicit, eliminating the parent-side copy of command assembly that creates a second place to repair.

text: Keep a two-case boundary pair for every byte and slice rule: a valid UTF-8 cut and an invalid-byte cut, stored as ordinary unittest inputs.
rationale: The pair forces retained-length and decoding behavior to surface together instead of paging later for an underspecified edge case.

text: Render raw failure evidence as a fixed-width line of input length, output length, slice bounds, and exit code from the existing test process.
rationale: The on-call view contains the arithmetic needed to fix cap and Gitstatus mistakes without an extra probe or parser.
